title: Who's who
note: Cast card for travellers who have never read the novel. Compiled by engine-tools 2026-08-19 from shared/personas/guide.md + passepartout.md and day-01-london/research/fact-sheet.md. One plain-English sentence each; `sources` (F-ids) are for reviewers — the player never shows or speaks them.

entries.name: Phileas Fogg
entries.who: The hero of the story: a rich London gentleman who lives his whole day by the clock, and who bets half his fortune — twenty thousand pounds — that he can travel around the world in eighty days.

entries.name: Passepartout
entries.who: Fogg's new French servant, a former circus acrobat from Paris who takes the job on the very morning the story begins because he wants a quiet life — and gets the opposite.

entries.name: Jules Verne
entries.who: The French author who invented Fogg: he published this story chapter by chapter in a Paris newspaper in late 1872, timed so Fogg's deadline fell just as the final chapters appeared.

entries.name: Sheridan
entries.who: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, a famous Irish playwright who really lived on Savile Row: Verne name-drops him to make Fogg's address feel real — and gets both the house number and the year of his death wrong.

entries.name: The five whist partners
entries.who: Fogg's card-playing friends at the Reform Club — Stuart an engineer, Sullivan and Fallentin bankers, Flanagan a brewer, and Ralph a director of the Bank of England — who together bet him twenty thousand pounds that he will fail.

entries.name: Thomas Cook
entries.who: A real English travel agent: while Verne was writing, Cook was leading the first commercial round-the-world tour — 222 days, heading west just as the fictional Fogg heads east.

entries.name: George Francis Train
entries.who: A real American showman who went around the world in 1870 — home in 164 days — and spent years afterwards claiming that Verne's hero was really him.
